subject: Units calibration: tokens vs characters vs requests — pilot pricing follow-up
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Jamal Ortiz <jamal.ortiz@brightcart.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Apr 2025 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up: BrightCart search proof-of-concept

Hi Jamal — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and a couple of trapped-down asks so we can price a short pilot accurately.

Recap (high level)
- Scope: search autocomplete + contextual site chat + nightly batch embeddings (re-rank) for top 500 SKUs.
- Primary success criteria: reduce failed or zero-result searches by 35% and lift SERP CTR for AI suggestions.
- Timeline: 6-week pilot, then production decision.

What's blocking our first-pass pricing: units and billing model clarity. During the call there was some confusion between tokens, characters, and API requests, and how prompt caching affects billed usage. Below I tried to distill the differences and then ask for some simple numbers so I can give you a target $/1M tokens estimate and a pilot cost.

Short definitions (practical)
- Token: the model's atomic unit (what we're billed on). For English text, a very rough rule of thumb is ~1 token per 4 characters (so 100 characters ~ 25 tokens) but this varies with punctuation/language.
- Character: literal characters in a string; useful for front-of-house sizing but not what the model billing uses.
- Request: one API call. A single request can include prompt tokens + response tokens; billed tokens = prompt tokens + generated (and any returned) tokens.
- Cache hit: if Redwood returns an answer from cache (prefix match/full response cached), no model call -> typically no billed tokens. If we cache embeddings or re-rank results locally, those compute costs may be outside model billing depending on setup.

Two quick examples I will use below (very simplified):
- Short autocomplete: prompt = 12 tokens, response = 6 tokens -> billed = 18 tokens.
- Chat turn: full prompt (history + user) = 220 tokens, response = 90 tokens -> billed = 310 tokens.

Action items for you (one-line answers please)
1) Expected weekly active users (WAU) for the pilot (estimate acceptable).
2) Avg search/autocomplete requests per WAU per week (ballpark).
3) Approx % of search queries you think map to templated prompts (eligible for prefix caching) vs unique prompts.
4) Any budget range for the pilot or a target $/1M tokens you want us to hit (helps decide hosted vs dedicated).

Attached: BrightCart_MVP_usage_estimate.xlsx — please fill columns 1–4 above and send back. Once I have numbers I will reply with a worked cost table showing $/1M tokens, estimated billed tokens per week, and a recommended pilot configuration.

Thanks —
Sofia Ivanova

Subject: Re: Quick follow-up: BrightCart search proof-of-concept — worked examples + pilot mapping

Hi Jamal — great, thanks for the sheet and the budget range. Below are three worked examples using the estimates you provided and a couple of conservative assumptions. I kept the math explicit so you can drop numbers in easily.

Assumptions & conversion rules we used here
- Token ≈ 4 characters (English). This is a heuristic for sizing; we will measure exact tokenization during the pilot and adjust.
- Billed tokens = tokens in the request sent to model (prompt tokens) + tokens generated by model (response).
- Cache behavior: if Redwood serves a response from an exact-match cache (prefix/full response), there is no model call -> no billed tokens. If you only cache embeddings or post-process results, model calls still bill tokens.
- Pricing scenarios: I show two $/1M token targets (conservative and stretch). We'll map your $8k–$12k pilot to those.

Flow A — Autocomplete (templated, high cache potential)
- User text: 35 chars ≈ 9 tokens.
- Templated prompt + static context: 40 chars ≈ 10 tokens.
- Model response (small suggestion list): ≈ 6 tokens.
Case 1: cache hit for templated prompt (60% of requests) -> billed tokens for those requests = 0.
Case 2: cache miss (40%) -> billed tokens ≈ prompt 19 + response 6 = 25 tokens/request.
Net expected billed tokens per request = 0.6*0 + 0.4*25 = 10 tokens/request.

Flow B — Conversational chat (stateful)
- User + trimmed history: 420 chars ≈ 105 tokens.
- System prompt + context: 120 chars ≈ 30 tokens.
- Model response: 120 tokens.
Billed tokens per chat turn ≈ 255 tokens. (Caching usually not effective here for new messages.)

Flow C — Nightly batch re-rank (embeddings + re-rank)
- Batch input: 6000 chars ≈ 1500 tokens.
- Re-rank prompts + generation (per item) variable; for 500 SKUs we assume 100 tokens generated across calls per SKU amortized -> +50,000 tokens.
Billed tokens per nightly job ≈ 51,500 tokens (this is dominated by generation work).

Mapping to your WAU and pilot numbers (using your sheet):
- Pilot WAU: 2,400 (from your sheet)
- Avg weekly autocomplete requests per WAU: 12 -> total weekly autocomplete requests = 28,800 -> billed tokens ~ 28,800 * 10 = 288,000 tokens
- Chat requests/week: 3 per WAU -> 7,200 requests -> billed tokens ~ 7,200 * 255 = 1,836,000 tokens
- Nightly batch: 1 job/week -> 51,500 tokens
Total billed tokens/week ≈ 2,175,500 tokens (~2.18M) -> monthly (~4.3 weeks) ≈ 9.36M tokens/month.

Costing examples (rounded)
- If target = $100 / 1M tokens -> monthly cost ≈ 9.36 * $100 = $936. That seems low vs your stated budget, so validation: our target $/1M needs to be higher for your $8k–$12k pilot.
- If target = $1,000 / 1M tokens -> monthly cost ≈ 9.36 * $1,000 = $9,360 -> aligns with your upper pilot range (note: $1k / 1M tokens implies higher per-token priority SLA / Dedicated-like pricing).

Implied $/1M range for $8k–$12k pilot (monthly) given our estimate of ~9.36M tokens/month:
- $8,000 / 9.36 ≈ $855 per 1M tokens
- $12,000 / 9.36 ≈ $1,282 per 1M tokens

Takeaways / recommendations
- Given the high chat volume, two levers will move cost most: (1) improve prompt compression (reduce history tokens sent); (2) increase templated caching for autocomplete to push more of the 28,800 weekly requests off the model. Even a 20% lift in cache hit reduces ~57k tokens/week.
- With your $8k–$12k pilot target, the implied $/1M token target falls roughly in the $850–$1,300 band. If you want to hit the lower end (~$100/1M), we'd need significant additional caching + fewer chat turns per WAU.
- For pilot packaging: we recommend hosted + a temporary pilot discount to validate traffic (~1 month) or a short Dedicated reservation if you want predictability and lower per-token price at higher commit. We'll model both if you prefer.

Next steps
1) If the math looks directionally correct, confirm whether you want us to model: (A) hosted with pilot credit + discount to hit $850/1M, or (B) Dedicated commit estimate for a target $600/1M (we'll run numbers).
2) We will instrument tokenized logging in the pilot so exact token:char ratios are measured and you get a true billed-usage forecast mid-pilot.
3) I'll pull together a one-page pilot pricing worksheet with estimated invoices under both (A) and (B).

I've attached our pricing worksheet (redwood-pricing-worksheet.csv) and populated the numbers above into the shared Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AbCdeFG-print

If you want, we can have a short 20-min call Monday to walk finance through the numbers and pick the pilot packaging.
